title: wrong component photographed
why:
A perfectly sharp, perfectly exposed photograph of the REAR caliper. Nothing is wrong with the evidence except that it is not evidence of this step.

OBSERVED, 27 Aug — same shape as photo-of-a-screen-refused. The Inspector returns ADD_FIELD at 0.3, so the step does not advance and nothing false is recorded. Its rationale is that the caliper sits over the disc and obscures the pad faces, which is a true statement about the photograph and not the reason it is wrong. It does not identify the component as the REAR caliper. Front and rear calipers on this machine are visually near-identical in isolation, so this is a limit of judging a component from one frame with no surrounding context, not a prompt that can be sharpened into it.

step.title: Fit the new pads and torque the caliper bolts
step.explanation: An under-torqued caliper bolt backs out under braking heat and the caliper moves. This is the step that kills someone if it is skipped.

field.prompt: Photograph the new pads seated in the caliper before the wheel goes back on
field.acceptance_description: both new pads in place in the FRONT caliper, friction material thick and unworn, close enough that the pad faces can be seen
field.guidance: Get close, get the caliper filling the frame, and make sure both pads are visible.
